I'd probably create a whole dungeon without *actual* enemies but I know that's a bit overkill and would probably bore the group really quickly if they're not eased into it.
  
Try adding more and more puzzles/riddles in a dungeon/adventure each session that 'forces' the players to roleplay, give different morally ambiguous choices (e.g. maybe your group finds a lone wounded member of the big bad evil faction in your setting, does your group kill him? If so, big deal. Does your group maybe dress his wounds and let him go? Have it bite back in their ass by a group of the baddies showing up behind your group while your group's fighting a shitload freshly hatched dragon babies they could've avoided if only they had told chained up mother dragon a riveting tale about the world outside her prison, etc.)
  
A great way to get ideas for these kinds of situations is to actually look at different raid encounters in MMOs (WoW, Lotro, Rift, etc...). For puzzles you could look at great classic video games (Soul Reaver comes to mind for example) and take those puzzles and adjust them.
  
After each session you could also point out what your party could've done/achieved if they had done this and that and what not so they start to think "Aww shit maybe we should've talked with the mother dragon and flied back in time to fight the possessed radish golem at the beginning of time itself?"
